argument: The retained mistake must be actual bridge geometry: a line approaches its old level, rises to a span, drops to the far bank, and reunites downstream. Roof edge, ground, and route need to share that order from different origins.

Hide labels, readout, supports, and bridge dots. A caption-free viewer should find repeated rises, suspended spans, drops, and far-bank returns in all three drawing systems. If it reads as an arch over an unchanged line, the mutation fails.

Pointer, Enter, and Space must create the same bounded bridge that changes the actual route field; lifting only the latest one must reproduce the exact prior geometry, including its span, height, drop, and reunite.

A bridge is an easy metaphor. Delete v012 if the line never crosses a real span, if the supports carry the meaning instead of the route, if edge input produces no structural change, or if the prose explains more memory than the drawing can show.
